title: Where to invest in a marketing funnel
purpose: Compare three ways to grow buyers: more traffic, a better sign-up rate or better retention, using the same funnel numbers.
summary: A funnel turns 10,000 visitors into 2,000 sign-ups, 600 active users and 150 buyers. The deck compares three investments. Each deep dive works through the arithmetic of one choice and names what to measure before committing budget.
explanation: Every stage multiplies the stages after it, so the same improvement is worth a different number of buyers depending on where you make it.

learning_check.question: The sign-up rate rises from 20% to 30% and later rates stay the same. How many buyers do you get?
learning_check.answer: 225: 3,000 sign-ups, 900 active users, and 25% of them buy.

slides.heading: Double the visitors
slides.notes: At unchanged rates, twice the visitors give twice the buyers; new channels may convert at different rates.

visual.verdict: Check that new visitors convert like old ones.

slides.heading: Sign-up rate from 20% to 30%
slides.notes: Every later stage receives half as many people again, so buyers rise by half.

slides.heading: Grow value without new visitors
slides.notes: Retention changes value per buyer, not the number of buyers, so measure the repeat purchase rate first.

items: Measure how many buyers buy again
Value per buyer grows; buyer count does not
